A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SkyDiffusion study, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures throughout. Neither contains an appendix; both reference supplementary material that is not included. All supplied pages support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthesis experiments on CVUSA, CVACT, VIGOR-Chicago, and G2A-3, including quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v5 retains these original quantitative experiments, ablations, and qualitative synthesis results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the curved BEV projection, nearest-camera multi-to-one fusion, BEV-controlled diffusion architecture, and training objective. No procedural or model-component change is stated.

E1.justification: Both versions use CVUSA, CVACT, VIGOR-Chicago, and the same G2A-3 disaster-response, low-altitude UAV, and historical high-resolution image-synthesis tasks. Their data sources and scenario coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine baselines and their participation across datasets, including the missing VIGOR-Chicago entries for X-Seq and CDTE. Table 3 still compares against ControlNet. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated splits, image resolutions, evaluation metrics, training budget, and inference settings remain unchanged. v5 omits some BEV parameter specifications without stating replacement settings; this is a documentation loss under D1, not evidence of a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the direct-input, standard-BEV, curved-BEV, and multi-to-one ablations. Figures 6–7 retain the same qualitative examples and case analyses. References to further supplementary analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and qualitative results in Figures 5–7 are unchanged. For example, VIGOR-Chicago FID remains 45.29 for single-view SkyDiffusion and 31.90 for its multi-to-one ablation.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the curved-surface assumption, and the mathematical descriptions of projection, fusion, and diffusion are unchanged. No new or revised derivation, proof, or formal result appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same method, dataset, and performance claims, including the headline 8.67% SSIM increase and 21.50% FID reduction.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of domain alignment and occlusion handling, the limitation on consistently generating rooftop details, and the applicability arguments for the three G2A-3 tasks.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 removes λ=2 and H=1.5 for CVUSA, CVACT, and G2A-3, plus λ=10 for one-to-one VIGOR-Chicago mapping. These values are not relocated elsewhere in v5. The multi-to-one λ=0 setting, remaining implementation details, and code/data access link are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography changes from 48 to 56 works: nine are added, including OmniCity, geometry-guided one-to-many cross-view diffusion, and URBench; Shi et al.'s Geometry-guided street-view panorama synthesis from satellite imagery is removed. Citation coverage expands, but the surrounding discussion and research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 adds Section 7 acknowledgements, removes the author email block, and changes the corresponding-author designation. Most prose and the scientific section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 8 to page 7, accompanied by text reflow and spacing adjustments. All seven figure images and the structures and captions of the three tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4, v5 removes dataset-specific curvature and camera-height values needed to reproduce the central BEV transformation. The added citations and funding acknowledgement provide limited contextual and transparency benefits, but do not compensate for this reproducibility loss. The method and scientific evidence otherwise remain unchanged.
